passage: Ingrid sat cross-legged in front of the TV in Porto as an advert for face cream ended. The girls in it were thin, pale and glowing. In the dark screen she saw her own reflection, freckled arms and all. "I don't look like that," she said quietly. Her cousin Rafael, who edits pictures for a small magazine, looked up from his laptop. "Come here." He opened a photo of a model and dragged some sliders. The skin went smooth, the waist thinner, the colour lighter. "That's how it's made. Nobody looks like that, not even her." Ingrid looked at the screen, then at her arm. "Real people look all sorts of ways, tall, round, dark, pale," he said. "Watch the people on the tram tomorrow."

qa.q: What does Rafael do for work?
qa.a: He edits pictures for a small magazine.

qa.q: Why did Ingrid say quietly, "I don't look like that"?
qa.a: She felt insecure, comparing herself with the girls in the advert and seeing her own freckled reflection in the dark screen.

qa.q: What could Ingrid do next time an advert makes her feel that way?
qa.a: She can remember that pictures are edited and look at the real people around her, who look all sorts of ways. 🙂

qa.q: How might Rafael see Ingrid's remark?
qa.a: He knows how much editing goes into such pictures, so he probably felt concerned and wanted to show her what is behind them.

grounding: Illustrates a child feeling not good enough beside edited media images and learning that images are edited and real people vary.
